storyline.label: DeepSeek Pro
storyline.latest_title: DeepSeek launches V4 Pro model with enhanced AI agent capabilities - news.cgtn.com

prior_narrative.tldr: DeepSeek's retrained V4-Flash overtook the company's own flagship V4 Pro on nine agent benchmarks in late July, then a refreshed "V4 Pro 0813" build quietly appeared on OpenRouter before DeepSeek officially confirmed it as a deliberate release. That confirmation left the agent-benchmark question unresolved and no changelog published.
prior_narrative.whats_new: The official V4 Pro launch also brought a sharp user-price increase and a preview-exit pitch built around unspecified "agent gains," per Nikkei Asia and Technology Org.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: The price hike changes the cost math that made V4 Pro competitive against V4-Flash and other cheap agent models, and the vague "agent gains" claim needs your own benchmark run before you treat it as resolving July's Flash-beats-Pro result.

status.detail: DeepSeek's confirmed V4 Pro release exited preview citing agent-capability gains, alongside a Nikkei Asia report of sharply higher user pricing.

beats.headline: Retrained V4-Flash beats flagship V4 Pro on nine agent benchmarks
beats.summary: DeepSeek's cheaper Flash variant overtakes the company's own Pro model on agent-focused evaluations.

beats.headline: A new "V4 Pro 0813" build appears on OpenRouter with no announcement
beats.summary: Simon Willison spots the refreshed Pro model listed API-only, with no DeepSeek announcement page to explain what changed.

beats.headline: Early hands-on says the refreshed Pro's multimodal capabilities meet expectations
beats.summary: The first outside impression of the new build focuses on multimodal quality rather than the agent-benchmark gap Flash had opened.

beats.headline: DeepSeek officially confirms the V4 Pro release
beats.summary: Outlets report the Aug 12 OpenRouter build as a deliberate, confirmed expansion release rather than a quiet leak.

beats.headline: Official launch comes with sharply higher user prices
beats.summary: Nikkei Asia reports the confirmed release raises per-user pricing, without breaking out the new rate versus V4-Flash.

beats.headline: V4 Pro exits preview status, DeepSeek cites agent-capability gains
beats.summary: The preview-exit framing points at agent gains but no benchmark numbers accompany the claim yet.

open_questions: Does the preview-exit build's claimed "agent gains" reclaim the benchmark lead V4-Flash took in July, or does Flash remain the stronger agent option?
What benchmark or evaluation backs the "agent gains" claim behind V4 Pro's preview exit?
How large is the new price increase, and does it still make Pro cheaper than V4-Flash per token for agent workloads?
Does DeepSeek publish a technical changelog for V4 Pro 0813 beyond the multimodal- and agent-capability claims?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Re-run your agent benchmark against the now-price-hiked V4 Pro 0813 build before trusting July's Flash-beats-Pro result, and pull the new per-token pricing before deciding whether Pro or Flash is the cheaper agent option.
